blast.cause: Caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae. Thrives in high humidity, frequent rain, and prolonged leaf wetness.
blast.treatment: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers. Improve field drainage. Apply systemic fungicides like Tricyclazole at early stages.

brownspot.cause: Caused by the fungus Bipolaris oryzae. It typically attacks crops in nutrient-depleted soils or during severe water stress.
brownspot.treatment: Apply balanced fertilizers, especially potassium. Treat seeds before planting and manage water levels consistently.

tungro.cause: Caused by a combination of viruses transmitted primarily by leafhoppers. Spreads rapidly when insect populations are high.
tungro.treatment: Control leafhopper populations using appropriate insecticides. Remove and destroy infected plants to prevent further spreading.

bacterialblight.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas bacteria. Often introduced through infected seeds and spread rapidly by wind-driven rain.
bacterialblight.treatment: Chemical controls are largely ineffective once established. Rely on resistant crop varieties and certified clean seeds.

early blight.cause: Caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. It spreads rapidly in warm temperatures accompanied by high humidity or heavy dews.
early blight.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves to prevent spread. Use copper-based protectant fungicides and practice strict crop rotation next season.

late blight.cause: Caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans. It is highly aggressive and spreads fast in cool, wet, and overcast conditions.
late blight.treatment: Immediately remove and destroy heavily infected plants. Apply specialized protectant fungicides and ensure excellent air circulation.

bacterial spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas species. Favored by high moisture and warm temperatures. Spreads rapidly via splashing rain.
bacterial spot.treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides early. Avoid overhead watering and ensure disease-free seeds are used for future planting.

leaf mold.cause: Caused by the fungus Passalora fulva. Predominantly affects crops in environments with poor air circulation and high relative humidity.
leaf mold.treatment: Increase spacing between plants for better airflow. Avoid overhead watering. Prune dense foliage and apply appropriate fungicides.

septoria.cause: Caused by the fungus Septoria lycopersici. Spreads through splashing water transferring the pathogen from contaminated soil to lower leaves.
septoria.treatment: Apply mulch to prevent soil splashing. Remove infected lower leaves immediately and use targeted fungicidal sprays.

spider mite.cause: Infestation by tiny arachnids. The damage is heavily exacerbated by hot, dry, and dusty environmental conditions.
spider mite.treatment: Spray plants with water to increase humidity and physically wash off mites. Use insecticidal soaps or horticultural oils for severe infestations.

target spot.cause: Caused by the fungus Corynespora cassiicola. Thrives in high humidity and moderate to warm temperatures.
target spot.treatment: Improve airflow through careful pruning. Avoid overhead irrigation and apply targeted fungicides at the first sign of lesions.

mosaic.cause: A highly contagious viral infection. It is most often spread mechanically through contaminated gardening tools, hands, or infected plant debris.
mosaic.treatment: There is no cure for infected plants. Remove and destroy them immediately. Wash hands and disinfect all tools thoroughly.

yellow leaf curl.cause: A viral disease transmitted primarily by the silverleaf whitefly. Severe in warm climates with high whitefly populations.
yellow leaf curl.treatment: Control whitefly populations using sticky traps or insecticidal soaps. Remove infected plants immediately to limit the spread of the virus.

healthy.cause: No pathogens detected. Environmental conditions and soil nutrition are currently optimal.
healthy.treatment: Maintain current watering schedules and fertilizer routines. Continue regular visual monitoring of the crop.
